subject: maths

concepts.title: Definition of Rational Numbers
concepts.definition: A number is considered rational if it can be expressed as a fraction where both the numerator and denominator are integers and the denominator is not zero.
concepts.key_idea: Any number that can be written in p/q form with q != 0.
question_patterns: is the number a rational number
write the following in p/q form
identify rational numbers from the list
can zero be a rational number
Can 5/7 be written with denominator 0?
Which of these are rational: 3/4, 0/5, a non-repeating endless decimal?

solution_steps.explain: Check if the number can be written as p/q where p and q are integers.
Ensure that the denominator q is not equal to zero.

concepts.title: Closure Property
concepts.definition: A set shows closure under an operation when combining any two of its members always lands back inside the same set.
concepts.key_idea: Sums, differences and products of two members stay members; a quotient can escape (zero divisor).
question_patterns: check if rational numbers are closed under addition
is subtraction closed for rational numbers
why is division not closed for rational numbers
verify closure property for multiplication
Is the quotient of two members always a member?
Fill in: rationals are closed under addition, subtraction and ___, but not ___.
Check closure: does 1/3 - 2/3 stay in the set?

solution_steps.explain: Add, subtract, or multiply the two given rational numbers.
Determine if the resulting value is also a rational number.

concepts.title: Commutative Property
concepts.definition: This property implies that the order in which two numbers are added or multiplied does not affect the final result.
concepts.key_idea: Swapping the two operands leaves the answer unchanged for these two operations.
question_patterns: verify commutativity for addition
is multiplication commutative for rational numbers
show that a + b equals b + a
check if subtraction is commutative
Show that 2/3 + 1/4 equals 1/4 + 2/3.
Does subtraction obey the swap rule for rationals?

solution_steps.explain: Compute the result of the operation in the first order (a + b).
Compute the result of the operation in the reversed order (b + a).

concepts.title: Associative Property
concepts.definition: The associative property states that when three or more numbers are added or multiplied, the way they are grouped does not change the sum or product.
concepts.key_idea: However you bracket three operands, the answer comes out the same.
question_patterns: verify associativity for addition
is multiplication associative for rational numbers
group the numbers to verify associativity
show that (a * b) * c = a * (b * c)
Does division obey the bracketing rule?

solution_steps.explain: Group the first two numbers and then operate with the third.
Group the last two numbers and then operate with the first.

concepts.title: Additive Identity
concepts.definition: Zero earns its title because combining it with any member leaves that member unchanged.
concepts.key_idea: Adding zero does not change the value of a number.
question_patterns: what is the additive identity of rational numbers
find the sum of a number and zero
identify the identity element for addition
verify the role of zero in addition
Find 5/6 + 0.
What does adding 0 do to -13/8?

solution_steps.explain: Add 0 to the given rational number a.

concepts.title: Multiplicative Identity
concepts.definition: One earns its title because multiplying any member by it changes nothing.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying by one preserves the original value.
question_patterns: what is the multiplicative identity
multiply a rational number by 1
identify the identity element for multiplication
verify the role of 1 in multiplication
Find 5/6 x 1.
What does multiplying by 1 do to -7/3?

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the given rational number a by 1.

concepts.title: Distributive Property
concepts.definition: The distributive property allows a number outside a set of parentheses to be multiplied by each term inside the parentheses separately.
concepts.formula: a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c
concepts.key_idea: Multiplication distributes over addition and subtraction.
question_patterns: solve using distributive property
simplify using distributivity
expand the expression a(b + c)
calculate using the distributive law
Evaluate 2/5 x (3/4 + 1/2) two different ways.
Expand 3/7 x (2/9 - 5/9) using the distributing rule.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the outer number a by the first inner number b.
Multiply the outer number a by the second inner number c.

concepts.title: Simplifying Expressions using Properties
concepts.definition: Reorder and regroup members so that easy pairings (same denominators, matching digits) happen first.
concepts.key_idea: Rearrange terms with common denominators to simplify calculations.
question_patterns: find the sum using properties
simplify the expression by rearranging terms
calculate the value of the following
use commutativity to solve
Simplify 3/7 + 5/9 + 4/7 + 4/9 by pairing.
Rearrange 2/5 x 7/3 x 5/2 for an easy product.

solution_steps.explain: Group terms that have common denominators or are easy to calculate.
Calculate the sum of the remaining terms.
Add the results of the groups together.

solution_template.explain: Bring terms with common factors together.
Subtract the remaining term from the result.
